# Sub2API 0.1.178.8 (czc-v2026.08.20.1)

This hotfix removes a benign Chinese software-engineering term from the effective second-layer candidate policy while preserving fail-closed handling for genuinely incomplete review evidence.

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Version | `0.1.178.8` |
| Version base | Official `0.1.178` |
| Previous production version | `czc-v2026.08.19.7` |
| Production tag | `czc-v2026.08.20.1` |
| Comparison | [`czc-v2026.08.19.7...czc-v2026.08.20.1`](https://github.com/zuchengchen/sub2api/compare/czc-v2026.08.19.7...czc-v2026.08.20.1) |

## Changes

- Retire the standalone Layer 2 candidate term `持久化`. It is common in benign database and software discussions and was the trigger in the affected account's false-positive review path.
- Filter the retired term from both built-in effective candidates and previously persisted custom candidate lists. The effective keyword policy advances from `keyword-v4` to `keyword-v5`, which also isolates prior candidate caches.
- Preserve the immutable v1, v2, and v3 moderation assets and their existing checksums. Filtering is applied by the runtime policy rather than by rewriting a released asset.
- Preserve fail-closed handling whenever matched evidence or surrounding contextual-review content is incomplete. The fix does not allow a reviewer to approve text it did not receive.
- Prevent incomplete evidence from replaying a cached verdict created by a complete request with the same bounded evidence hash, and separate complete/incomplete in-flight reviews.
- Do not publish cache entries for incomplete evidence, including blocked outcomes, because the bounded evidence hash does not identify omitted text.

## Compatibility And Upgrade

- No database schema or configuration-format migration is required. Existing configuration, API keys, moderation history, and application data are preserved.
- Persisted `keyword-v4` configuration is normalized to `keyword-v5` when loaded. Any persisted standalone `持久化` candidate is removed from the effective policy.
- Rollback to `0.1.178.7` restores the retired standalone candidate term and the earlier incomplete-evidence cache behavior; it does not alter stored data.

## Verification

Passed before release:

- Focused keyword-policy, incomplete-evidence, fail-closed, configuration, and cache-isolation regression tests.
- Full `internal/service` package tests with `go test -p 1 ./internal/service -count=1`.
- Full backend suite with `go test -p 1 ./... -count=1`.
- Moderation resource contract tests, including verification that the released v1/v2 assets retain their original SHA-256 checksums and v3 still inherits the 114/457 policy layers.
- Frontend production build with `corepack pnpm run build`; the existing dynamic-import and large-chunk warnings were non-fatal.
- Frontend lint and type checks with `corepack pnpm run lint:check` and `corepack pnpm run typecheck`.
- `gofmt` and `git diff --check`.

Pending deployment verification:

- Online binary version and SHA-256, systemd state, direct and nginx health endpoints, active configuration checksum, moderation audit results, and the two-entry local rollback list.

Failed or invalidated checks:

- The first full backend invocation was invalidated when the shared worktree was switched to another branch during test compilation; its generated test entry points no longer matched the checked-out files. The suite was rerun from the fixed hotfix commit as recorded above.

Skipped:

- Synthetic checks that send email, execute OAuth flows, or intentionally create external provider side effects.

## Deployment And Rollback

- Build from the immutable `main-czc` release tag using `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `-tags embed`, `-trimpath`, and `-buildvcs=false`, with version, commit, build time, build type, and release URL injected.
- Before replacement, archive the exact installed `0.1.178.7` binary with its metadata and SHA-256. Stage the candidate on the same filesystem and replace the executable atomically.
- Preserve configuration and data, restart only `sub2api.service`, then verify health, version metadata, moderation behavior, and rollback candidates.
- After successful deployment, retain only verified `0.1.178.7` and `0.1.178.6` local rollback binaries and remove staging/build files and deployment Go caches.
